articles.headline: Saints putting RB Travis Etienne (hamstring) on IR
articles.description: The Saints are placing running back Travis Etienne on injured reserve, which will sideline him for at least the next four games.
articles.body:
The New Orleans Saints are placing running back Travis Etienne Jr. on injured reserve, which will sideline him for at least the next four games.

Etienne has a hamstring injury he suffered in the Saints' Week 3 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders.

Etienne had been on the injury report leading up to the game with a hamstring issue but participated fully in Friday's practice. Coach Kellen Moore, who announced that Etienne would miss time with his injury, said the injury occurred on the same leg as the one that had been bothering him during the week.

Etienne had a season-high 19 carries for 57 yards before the injury. After he left, carries were split between Alvin Kamara (six carries after Etienne's injury) and Kendre Miller (four carries after Etienne's injury).

Kamara, who missed time with a knee injury in September, had nine carries in his season debut against the Baltimore Ravens in Week 2 over Etienne's eight carries, although the Saints almost exclusively used Etienne as the main rusher in the first half of the Raiders game.

Kamara, Miller and rookie CJ Donaldson will likely all be used in the Saints' Week 4 game against the Atlanta Falcons on Monday night. Kamara is second on the team with 18 carries for 51 yards despite missing the season opener, while Miller, who was a healthy inactive against the Ravens, is third with 13 carries for 44 yards and a touchdown.

articles.headline: Joey Porter happy for fresh start with Cowboys, eyes Sunday debut
articles.description: Joey Porter Jr. says he hopes to make his debut for the Cowboys on Sunday when they play the Texans.
articles.body:
FRISCO, Texas -- When the week began, Joey Porter Jr. thought he would be playing Thursday night for the Pittsburgh Steelers against the Cleveland Browns. Now, he hopes to make his Dallas Cowboys debut Sunday against the Houston Texans.

"We're just trying to take things day by day," Porter said after his first practice in Dallas, "and if everything looks good, then we should be out there."

Porter was at the movie theater watching Brad Pitt's "Heart of the Beast" when he got word of the trade. Early in the morning, he was on a plane to his new team, officially signifying the end of his run with the team that drafted him in the second round in of the 2023 draft.

The saga lasted throughout the offseason and into training camp as he awaited an extension that never came, while dealing with a back injury. Porter said it was more his call to not play in against the Browns, but that his back was, "feeling better," as he spoke to the media.

Porter is not listed on the Cowboys' injury report.

"It was a hard process, a lot of ups and downs," Porter said. "Definitely felt disrespected, definitely felt undervalued. But that's the old news now. That's how I look at it. I'm onto new beginnings, new chapters. And like I said, I'm a Cowboy. I'm in Dallas, so I'm happy about that."

The Cowboys gave up a 2027 sixth-round pick and a 2028 second rounder to acquire Porter, marking the third deal the organizations have made since May of 2025 (George Pickens, Broderick Jones).

But Porter will have to wait for an extension from the Cowboys, too. Still, Porter said he would be open to finishing his career in Dallas.

"I'm down with it if they are. I want to finish my career here," Porter said. "So hopefully I just perform like how I know how to perform and do what I do and I'm going to let everything take care of the rest."

Through three games, the Cowboys are 25th in points allowed (27.3) and 30th in yards (387). The Cowboys are one of four teams to have yet to record an interception.

With Cobie Durant (hamstring) expected to miss his second game and Shavon Revel not practicing much this week with knee and ankle issues, the Cowboys almost need to have Porter immediately.

"This is more about you get a chance to get a young corner that's got elite cover skills that can come in and add to a group that's depleted right now with injuries is always good," coach Brian Schottenheimer said. "But I think change of scenery is good."

It worked for Pickens, who had career highs in catches (93), yards (1,429) and touchdowns (nine) last year with the Cowboys.

Defensive coordinator Christian Parker used the term, "boundary eraser," when describing his evaluation of Porter when he came out of Penn State. While Porter has a reputation for his man-to-man skills, Parker said he saw him do enough work with the Steelers to know it won't be a difficult adjustment to the scheme. He said even if the Cowboys are in zone, they have some man principles.

articles.headline: NFL Week 4 uniforms: Browns wearing 'Alpha Dawg' look; Giants go 'Legacy'
articles.description: Here's a look at what each NFL team is wearing in Week 4, led by an alternate look from the Cleveland Browns.
articles.body:
As the calendar turns to October, NFL uniforms remain as fresh as ever with an alternate-heavy slate in Week 4. 

On "Thursday Night Football," the Cleveland Browns will wear their "Alpha Dawg" combination against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Cleveland revealed the all-brown threads in July 2025 with a brand new alternate brown helmet. They debuted last season and marked the first time in franchise history that a brown helmet was worn. Orange-colored numbers run across the front and back of the jersey, as well as on the shoulder. There's also an orange stripe on the helmet.

In the throwback space, the New York Giants are donning their legacy uniforms against the Arizona Cardinals. New York wore these threads from 1980 to 1999. It was reintroduced in 2022, when the team brought back the navy helmet. Other design elements include classic numbers plus the red-and-blue trim on the jerseys and pants, similar to the uniforms of the 1980s and '90s. Written inside the collar is "Once a Giants, Always a Giant," the words of late owner Wellington Mara. 

The Carolina Panthers, meanwhile, will bring an all-black look to "Sunday Night Football" against the Detroit Lions. Carolina first debuted this all-black combination in 2022. 

The Dallas Cowboys are rocking navy blue alternates with silver pants against the Houston Texans, a look the team will wear only a handful of times each season. The Texans will wear liberty white jerseys with deep steel blue pants. It marks the same uniform matchup the Texans and Cowboys wore for Houston's first regular-season game as a franchise in 2002.

articles.headline: Jalen Hurts challenges underdog Eagles to find out who they are ahead of matchup with Rams
articles.description: — Jalen Hurts isn't used to losing much with the Philadelphia Eagles — only 16 times since 2022 — and he certainly isn't used to getting embarrassed.
articles.body:
PHILADELPHIA -- — Jalen Hurts isn't used to losing much with the Philadelphia Eagles — only 16 times since 2022 — and he certainly isn't used to getting embarrassed.


              Yet from Hurts on down, the Eagles know that's exactly what happened in Chicago in a loss that essentially sent them into an existential crisis only three games into the season. Hurts said he left Chicago following a 27-7 loss with one question for an Eagles team that has not played to championship standards over its first three games.


              “Who are we?” Hurts said.


              Hurts was sacked twice and threw an interception against the Bears. The Eagles were limited to 62 yards of offense in the second half and 248 for the game. He also absorbed a late hit from linebacker D’Marco Jackson along the sideline.


              Hurts' performance was off. He knows the season is in his hands and it's up to him to help the Eagles straighten it out against the Los Angeles Rams.


              “I don’t really care how we look,” Hurts said. “I don’t care who we are. I want to be winners. I want to win, and that’s always going to take precedence over anything.”


              Hurts challenged the Eagles with a question of identity. 


              The battered Rams are in a bigger hole than the Eagles and yet they are modest road favorites in Philadelphia.


              Rams cornerback Jaylen Watson and tight end Terrance Ferguson likely to be sidelined. The Rams should receive a boost by the return of No. 1 wide receiver Puka Nacua after he missed the last two games because of a hip and groin injury.


              “It adds a great football player that’s a huge part of our offense,” coach Sean McVay said, “and it’s a big deal.”


              The connection between quarterback Matthew Stafford and wide receiver Davante Adams flourished for the second straight game without Nacua. Adams caught seven passes for 137 yards despite being covered by arguably the NFL’s cornerback in Patrick Surtain II.


              Can he keep up the stellar production if Nacua returns to the lineup?


              “Well, it doesn’t mean that it’s not going to happen again,” Adams said. “We never know exactly how the plays are going to get called or if he plays or if he doesn’t play.”

articles.headline: Arrowhead West no more? Raiders’ fast start could mean Chiefs feel less at home at Allegiant
articles.description: — Allegiant Stadium has been called Arrowhead West almost since it opened in 2020.
articles.body:
LAS VEGAS -- — Allegiant Stadium has been called Arrowhead West almost since it opened in 2020.


              The venue is awash in red when the Kansas City Chiefs visit Last Vegas each year and, at best, it feels like a neutral-site game for the Raiders. The moniker was particularly apt in February 2024 when the Chiefs occupied the Las Vegas locker room for the Super Bowl and practiced at the Raiders ' facility. 


              But this Sunday could be different when the two 3-0 teams face one another given Las Vegas' strong and unexpected start to the season. 


              "We know the Chiefs fans travel well,” Raiders star pass rusher Maxx Crosby said. “We have to earn having the full silver and black crowd. We've won three games, but we have a lot of work to do.”


              Crosby noted Raiders fans have already made their voices heard this season during games at the Los Angeles Chargers and New Orleans. The season opener against Miami was among the loudest Allegiant has been for a Raiders game.


              So it's possible this won't be a typical game against the Chiefs when it's difficult to tell which is the home team.


              Secondary market ticket seller Vivid Seats said it expects 64% of the crowd to back Las Vegas. StubHub reported, based on zip codes, that sales appear to be going to Raiders fans by a 4-to-1 ratio, though nearby Chiefs supporters could be responsible for a decent chunk as well.


              The Chiefs beat Las Vegas during the first five meetings at Allegiant before losing last season's finale 14-12 when both teams played a load of backups.


              It's a different situation this weekend. The Raiders, who have just one winning season since moving from Oakland, California, hope to show their start isn’t a fluke.


              Kansas City is looking to take back the AFC West after losing it last season to end its nine-year dominance of the division.


              "I love Chiefs fans traveling,” Kansas City quarterback Patrick Mahomes said. “Its always cool to see red in the stands and ‘home of the Chiefs’ at the end of the national anthem. I wouldn't be surprised if it's a very hostile environment, going back to the Oakland Raiders days. They're playing great football, you can see it on tape. That 3-0 record is real.”

              Kansas City (3-0) at Las Vegas (3-0).

The 2026-27 NBA season officially kicked off Sept. 22 as the Houston Rockets held their media day, before the Dallas Mavericks followed suit Friday.

The other 28 teams in the association joined them Monday, ahead of training camps beginning for most teams.

How will LeBron James and Jaylen Brown look in their new Philadelphia 76ers uniforms? What will Giannis Antetokounmpo's first media day away from Milwaukee look like? And how will the other new faces in new places make their first impressions?

Check back here for all the latest buzz, news and reactions from our ESPN NBA insiders, with the latest info at the top:

Depth charts | Trade machine | More

Oct. 1

Mitch Johnson excited about Billy Donovan's role with Spurs

San Antonio Spurs coach Mitch Johnson likes what he's seen so far at training camp from new lead assistant coach Billy Donovan.

"I don't want to be naive enough to think I'm going to tell you what a 61-year old Hall of Fame coach like Billy Donovan and his resume can bring to the table," Johnson said. "I'm excited he's here. He's a tremendous person, great personality, fits in seamlessly. He's got worlds of experience and he's an extremely hard worker. He's not kicking up his feet and telling stories. He's rolling his sleeves up and getting his hands dirty. He's going to help all of us and probably me, specifically, a ton this year."

Donovan joined the staff in July, replacing former lead assistant Sean Sweeney, who left San Antonio to take the head coaching job in Orlando. Sweeney ran the Spurs' defense last season, helping it improve from 25th to third in the NBA in defensive rating (110.4).

Donovan won't be tasked with taking on Sweeney's responsibilities, according to sources, however. San Antonio brought in Donovan to lean on his experience on both ends of the floor, as well as his vast knowledge of the NBA and college games.

A member of the Naismith Basketball Hall of Fame class of 2025, Donovan joined the Spurs after 11 seasons as an NBA coach with the Chicago Bulls and Oklahoma City Thunder, after capturing two college basketball national titles in 2006 and 2007 with the Florida Gators. -- Michael C. Wright

Guard Jamal Shead has agreed to a three-year, $24 million extension with the Toronto Raptors, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Shead averaged 6.6 points and 5.6 assists per game last season.

articles.headline: Manchester City guilty charges explained: Premier League's options, how appeal works, more
articles.description: Tuesday's news that the Premier League found Man City guilty of 100-plus charges of breaking financial rules is a landmark moment. But what comes next: what punishments are on the table, and how does the appeals process work?
articles.body:
Manchester City's guilty verdict on 114 charges of breaking Premier League financial rules is a landmark moment in global sport.

City continues to assert their innocence and have signaled their intention to appeal before Friday's deadline. But the Independent Commission's verdict could hardly have been more damning, accusing the club of "sham" contracts involving its Abu Dhabi owners as part of a "disguised funding scheme" that contributed to inflating revenues and reducing costs by over £900 million. Witnesses in City's defense were accused of dishonesty, and the club was found to have "clearly intended to circumvent" Premier League rules.

The breaches relate specifically to a nine-year period (2009-18), but the shockwaves permeate far beyond. Pep Guardiola's trophy-laden legacy is in doubt. The Premier League's reputation and viability is in the balance. Rivals may seek retribution through compensation claims, triggering challenges that could last for years.

Meanwhile, City's punishment is yet to be determined. Under Section W, Rule 54 of the Premier League's Handbook, they are facing a punishment ranging from a reprimand to expulsion. There could be a fine, a points deduction and a transfer ban.

City's aggressive protestations of innocence only contribute to the widespread uncertainty and reduces the likelihood of all parties coming together to reach agreement on a settlement for the time being. Beyond that, the legal complexities are vast.

ESPN has spoken with one of the United Kingdom's leading law firms, Howard Kennedy, in pursuit of clarity. Partners Kyle Phillips and Lois Langton head the firm's sports group, with Phillips specializing in business crime and regulatory process. On Thursday, the pair talked with ESPN's James Olley to answer some basic questions and follow-ups about what this all means and what's next.

Editor's note: This interview has been edited for clarity and length.

How would you characterize the commission's findings?

Kyle Phillips: I think it's worse than many people expected. The words that were used by the commission in the findings report, caveated with the fact it's very difficult to read because a lot of it is redacted and there's no evidence or appendices that they keep referring to, but the language that they use is very strong.

"Sham" is one point. You've got the disguised payments, sorry -- the "disguised funding scheme," overstating commercial revenue, the amounts involved ... it is all quite shocking. And it is quite a strong statement to say that you find the witness evidence that was given to be "dishonest" -- a powerful word in any decision.

In any regulatory proceedings, it takes a lot for them to use that word.
